title: KV ramp-and-hold throughput probe with anomaly scoring for early regression detection
creator: Priya Kumar
description: Create a repeatable 'ramp-and-hold' load probe for the KV/prefix cache that captures throughput (tokens/sec), p95/p99 tail latencies, hit-rate, memory footprint, and an anomaly score over time. The goal is an automated early-warning signal for regressions introduced by kernel changes, allocation tweaks, or cache policy changes without needing full-blown stress runs. Outputs feed into CI gating and the Console regression dashboard.
background: Current KV cache efforts (hotset, prefetch, occupancy) have good offline simulations, but we lack a compact, fast test that: 1) exercises realistic arrival patterns, 2) correlates hit-rate -> latency -> memory in a way that surfaces small regressions, and 3) produces a single anomaly score that can be trended in PRs and nightly runs. Existing artifacts are long-running stress harnesses; this probe should run in ~15-30 minutes per configuration and be stable across infra noise.
proposed_solution: Implement a three-phase probe: a) ramp-up: linear increase to target RPS over 5 minutes to expose scheduling and cold-start inefficiencies, b) hold: maintain steady-state for 15 minutes to collect stable p50/p95/p99 and KV hit metrics, c) tear-down: graceful drop for resource cleanup and eviction observation. Compute an anomaly score combining p95 delta, hit-rate delta, and memory delta vs. baseline using weighted z-scores. Publish metrics to the Console ingestion endpoint and emit a summary JSON for CI that includes tokens/sec, p95, p99, hit-rate, resident memory, and anomaly_score.
test_plan: 1) Implement load driver script (go/python) that can replay synthetic prefix distributions and live-mirror sampled production traffic. 2) Provide configuration matrix: sequence length distributions (short/medium/long), hotset skew levels (zipf s=0.6, 0.9), and memory caps. 3) Run baseline on known-good runtime build to record fingerprints. 4) Add automatic regression detection step: compute anomaly_score and fail if > threshold for two consecutive runs or if p95 increases > 15% while hit-rate decreases > 3%. 5) Add canary gate integration in CI where PRs to runtime trigger the probe on a small dedicated nodepool. 6) Bake graphs and alerts into Console using the "kv-ramp-probe" dashboard.
metrics:
- tokens_per_sec (instant + avg over hold)
- p50/p95/p99 generation latency (ms)
- KV prefix cache hit_rate (pct)
- resident_memory_bytes (MB)
- pkgs_allocated_during_run (counts)
- anomaly_score (unitless)
- sample_trace_ids_for_p95_events (list)
acceptance_criteria:
- Probe code checked in with config-driven targets and documented runbook.
- Baseline fingerprint collected and stored in artifacts/GCS with timestamped keys.
- CI step passes on known-good build and fails on synthetic regression build (we will simulate +20% p95 via token delay injection to validate).
- Console dashboard exists with trend panel for anomaly_score + decomposed metrics.
- Alert rule documented: anomaly_score > 3 OR (p95 delta > 15% AND hit_rate delta < -3%) triggers paging to oncall.
